subject: Pipeline oscillation: customer impact, internal remediation plan & customer note
messages:
From: Charlie Dunn <charlie@fastmart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-04T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Unexpected latency/throughput oscillation hitting checkout

Jordan —

We started seeing large variability on gen API p99 latencies and periodic drops in throughput this morning between 08:50–09:05 PT. Behavior looks like short bursts where a subset of requests hit 3–5s p95 and overall TPS drops ~40% for 1–2 minute windows. It’s impacting checkout throughput and causing retries on our side.

Attached a small set of request ids and sampled traces (request_logs.tar.gz). We can keep traffic reduced for a while if you need to triage. Please let me know next steps and ETA for a mitigation.

— Charlie
Ops Lead, FastMart
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Charlie Dunn <charlie@fastmart.com>
Date: 2027-12-04T09:24:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected latency/throughput oscillation hitting checkout

Folks — forwarding Charlie's note. He sent sample logs. Symptoms: short periodic drops in TPS and p99 spikes localized to their checkout traffic. They are running on our hosted API in us-west-2, mostly gen endpoints using the 8k-context variant pinned in their account.

Initial asks:
- Ben / SRE: can you triage whether this looks like scheduling / multi-tenant eviction or KV-cache churn? Ben, what telemetry should we pull first?
- Marcus / Eng: please check runtime hot-paths (kernel scheduling, batch fusion) for signs of oscillation with their request shape.
- Marissa / Product: I'll need a short outbound note for Charlie within 90 minutes with current mitigation and ETA. Prefer one concise status update, not an engineering dump.

I’ll assemble a brief internal timeline and post updates here.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-04T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected latency/throughput oscillation hitting checkout

Quick triage notes — I pulled the customer's request traces and infra metrics. Early signal:
- Sporadic CPU saturations on a small subset of pods serving their tenant. These line up with the ~1–2 minute windows.
- KV cache hit-rate drops concurrently for those pods (evictions observed).
- We also saw increased tail latency in the kernel queuing metric (suggests short-lived contention on kernel-side scheduling).

Hypothesis: workload fanout + cold KV-cache regen causing transient overload on a subset of workers which then triggers fallbacks and reduces effective throughput.

Immediate actions I'm proposing:
1) Apply a temporary routing pin to shift ~30% of the customer's traffic to a warm pool (same model family) to reduce concentrated fanout pressure.
2) Increase KV-cache eviction threshold for the affected nodes to avoid aggressive cache churn.
3) Open SRE-912 and attach traces (I've created the ticket).

I can execute 1) and 2) now (need approval from product for any routing exception). Expected mitigation observable within 10–15 minutes after roll.

Ben
Staff SRE
(attachment: prod-error-snippets.txt)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Charlie Dunn <charlie@fastmart.com>
Date: 2027-12-04T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected latency/throughput oscillation hitting checkout

Thanks Ben — sounds like a sensible short-term mitigation. Jordan / Marcus: two product/roadmap points to capture while we remediate:
- Can we document a safe routing-exception guardrail for customer-directed pins (duration, impact analysis, rollback)? This would help Sales/CS during incidents.
- We should add a small engineering story to evaluate KV-cache adaptive thresholds based on per-tenant request fanout. Not full work now, just capture as a Q1 candidate.

Jordan — for the customer brief I suggest: short summary, what we’re changing now, expected observable impact, and next steps + ETA for follow-up postmortem. I’ll draft a one-paragraph note and attach it as customer-brief-draft.docx for your review.

Marissa
Principal PM, Serving Platform
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Charlie Dunn <charlie@fastmart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-04T10:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency/throughput oscillation hitting checkout

Charlie — quick update: thanks for the logs. Our SREs have identified transient KV-cache churn on a subset of workers that aligns with the windows you saw. We’re rolling a short-lived routing pin to redistribute ~30% of your requests to a warm pool and increasing the KV eviction threshold on the affected nodes.

What to expect in next 15 minutes:
- You should see reduced p99 spikes and more consistent throughput; we’ll monitor and report back.
- We will not change your pinned model version — only routing and cache heuristics for a short window.

Next steps and timeline:
- 10:45 PT: mitigation roll initiated (in progress).
- 11:10 PT: preliminary verification and follow-up note to you with metrics.
- Full postmortem and remediation plan (including the product asks Marissa mentioned) within 72 hours.

If you prefer we can schedule a quick 15-min bridge — otherwise I’ll send the verification note after we confirm stabilization.

— Jordan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
(attachments: customer-brief-draft.docx)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Charlie Dunn <charlie@fastmart.com>
Date: 2027-12-04T16:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected latency/throughput oscillation hitting checkout — status update

Final status for today:
- Routing pin rolled at 10:45 PT and KV eviction thresholds adjusted.
- Observed stabilization: p99 reduced from intermittent 3–5s to steady ~650ms for the sampled windows; throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline.
- Affected nodes show lower eviction rates and kernel queuing subsided.

Open items:
- Engineering follow-up: Marcus to own a short spike-proofness story to harden batch fusion/scheduling in the next sprint.
- Product follow-up: Marissa to define routing-exception guardrails and capture a Q1 roadmap ticket for adaptive KV thresholds.
- Postmortem: I’ll attach traces and timeline to SRE-912 and we’ll aim to publish within 72 hours.

Thanks everyone for quick turn. Charlie — please let us know if you see any recurrence; we’ll keep SRE-912 updated.

Ben
Staff SRE
